$comment: The single source of truth for this project's values. Build scripts read it via build/lib/project-config.mjs; the maker/checker agents read it directly. Nothing else should restate these values. Run `npm run init` to fill it in.

odc.$comment: Where the LIVE theme is served, so `npm run check:live-theme` can prove the hand-pasted ODC theme still matches this repo. Deliberately `null` rather than a substitutable placeholder: the environment does not exist on day one, and a scaffold that fails its build over a URL nobody could have filled in yet trains people to ignore the gate. While these are null the check exits 0 with 'not configured'. Fill them in after the theme is first published — the URL pattern is <environmentUrl>/<appModule>/css/<odcThemeModule>.<themeName>.css. Use the STABLE, un-fingerprinted URLs; a URL that changes every publish makes the check a chore and it gets switched off.

conventions.$comment: THREE-STATE, never a bare value. status: confirmed | assumed | TBD. A convention that is not `confirmed` is NOT A RULE: the checker must not enforce it and must not raise findings against it. This exists because a previous template shipped `Spacing base: 4pt` as a plausible default nobody had verified — the loop then flagged every value that wasn't a multiple of 4, manufacturing false-positive findings and a bug that had to be closed as not-planned. A credible-looking default is worse than a blank. Promote to `confirmed` only when the designer or brand owner has actually said so.
